paragraphs.text: The belief instrument was demonstrated by an explicit-stance positive control at the earlier single-seed, instrument-specific reading. This point estimate was derived from recorded arm scores without an inferred interval; its token dose was lower than that of the evidence corpus, and it does not establish general belief transfer. At the later reading, the same positive-control contrast decayed while the matched-control-netted evidence-only contrast rose. The earlier evidence-only reading was positive despite being quoted in earlier drafts as the near-null cell; it used a matched off-topic control, all arms gated, and a single seed. With the same arms and control later, the evidence-only contrast was larger, supporting a slow rather than inert interpretation. All seven arms gated, and because the control passed at the recorded threshold, the late-step gate failure was genuinely late. The deterministic table pairs each belief ratio with its optimizer-step reading.
